AI Engineer is LinkedIn’s #1 fastest-growing job two years running, paying $206K. But the popular “deep learning roadmap” covers only ~22% of what employers screen for. Here’s the real one.
Press enter or click to view image in full size

The $206K AI Engineer Job Is 80% Software Engineering. Most Roadmaps Teach the Wrong Role.There’s a painful pattern playing out in thousands of self-taught careers right now. Someone reads that AI Engineer is the hottest, best-paid job in tech — which is true — and dutifully starts the roadmap everyone recommends: linear algebra, then calculus, then neural networks, then building a transformer from scratch in PyTorch. Twelve months later they’re competent at training models… and they freeze when asked to ship a reliable retrieval system to production, because that — not model training — is the actual job. They studied hard for the wrong role.
The numbers make the stakes concrete. The average US AI Engineer earned $206,000 in 2025 — a roughly $50,000 jump in a single year — and LinkedIn ranked AI Engineer the #1 fastest-growing job title for both 2025 and 2026, back-to-back years at the top. Demand is running well ahead of supply. By every hiring metric, this is the highest-leverage entry point in software in over a decade.
